findings.title: Dry-run and lint-write path lists are hand-maintained copies of what the installers write
findings.description:
`INSTALL_PATHS` hard-codes `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude`, `.cursor`, `.github`, `.agents`, and the manifest dir. The change removes `propagateDirs` from `TARGETS`, so these lists no longer derive from one definition. `AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` still exists in `ideTargets.ts` and `.agents` is repeated here as a literal.

`LINT_WRITE_PATHS` in `paths.ts` repeats the literal file names that `lint.ts` writes (`ruff.toml`, `analysis_options.yaml`, `eslint.config.mjs`, `.editorconfig`, `Directory.Build.props`). I checked that the two currently agree, but nothing enforces it.

A new target, or a new lint output missing from either list, would drop out of the dry-run preview with no error or warning. That breaks the CLAUDE.md rule to define each value once and reference it everywhere. Derive the dry-run list from `TARGETS` (marker files plus an install-dirs field) and from shared constants that `lint.ts` also uses. Alternatively, add a test that fails when an install writes a path outside these lists.

findings.title: `isFilesystemError` classifies any Error with a string `code` as an install failure, not a bug
findings.description:
`isFilesystemError` accepts any `Error` with a string `code`, and `installIde` turns a match into `exitCode: 1` (lines 91-95). Node also sets string codes on non-filesystem errors, such as `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE` and `ERR_FS_CP_EINVAL`. A programming bug that throws one of those would be reported as an ordinary failed install. The stack would be lost, and in `installWorktrees` the loop would carry on to the next worktree.

The doc comments here and on `installWorktrees` say "any other exception is a bug and propagates", which this check doesn't guarantee. The test "stops on any other exception" mocks `installIde` itself, so it never exercises this classification.

Narrow the check to an allowlist of errno codes (`EACCES`, `ENOSPC`, `ENOENT`, `EPERM`, `EEXIST`, `EROFS`, …), or to codes that start with `E` but not `ERR_`. Add a test that drives `installIde` with a real non-filesystem error.

findings.title: `python()` in `lint.ts` is long and branchy
findings.description: The method runs to roughly 55 lines and handles three config sources: standalone ruff config, `pyproject.toml`, and the layered `extend` case. That is slightly over the ~50-line guideline. Splitting out the "write extending ruff.toml" branch would shorten it.

findings.title: Intentional output changes for #38 and #40
findings.description: `getApplyTo` now returns `**` once instead of `**\n**`. `replaceBlock` now keeps a missing final newline. Both diverge from the guide's bash behavior. They are documented in comments and the snapshots were updated, including a changed manifest CRC for `broken.instructions.md`. Existing copilot installs will see a one-time rewrite of rules that have no `paths:`. Mention this in the changelog.

findings.title: `realGuide.test.ts` needs the guide submodule checked out
findings.description: The test reads `project-documents/ai-project-guide` under `REPO_ROOT`. The guide is present in this worktree, so it should work here. In a checkout where the submodule isn't initialized, it will fail with "install exited 1" rather than a clear "guide missing" message. A precondition check with a descriptive error would help.

findings.title: Native installer replaces the bash script and worktree propagation
findings.description:
I grepped `packages/` and found no remaining references to `guideScript`, `propagateToWorktrees`, `readManifest`, `parseManifestLine`, `manifestTempPath`, `ManifestEntry`, `propagateDirs` or `generatedPromptDirs`. The `Record<Target, …>` typing is preserved in `TARGETS` and `TARGET_SETUP`. The legacy `.prompt.md` sweep moved into the copilot installer, guarded by `GENERATED_MARKER` (`targets/copilot.ts:75-85`). Worktrees are installed from the main checkout's guide, each with its own `rules.exclude`.

The new `setup-ide.test.ts` covers the arguments passed to the installer, alias normalization, a failing worktree not stopping the others, non-install exceptions stopping the loop, and the overwrite prompt for all four targets. `parseRulesExclude` is centralized in core and reused by the validator.
